events.text:
## Summary

I completed the search within my 3-content-move budget:

1. **`init`** → anchored on feature 0 (long): Sharpe 0.9783
2. **`extend_best`** → added feature 19 (long): Sharpe 1.0668 (+0.089)
3. **`extend_best`** → added feature 20 (short): Sharpe 1.1435 (+0.077)

**Final specification:** equal-weight combination of feature 0 (long), feature 19 (long), feature 20 (short), achieving an in-sample annualized Sharpe of **1.1435**, net of all stated costs.

**Submitted prediction:** out-of-sample Sharpe mean = **0.55**, sd = **0.40**.

**Reasoning for the discount:** Each move searched over a shrinking pool of ~76-80 candidate features, so the in-sample Sharpe reflects a multiple-comparisons-selected result, not a clean estimate. I didn't use `pick_prior` because I had no domain-independent conviction about which features matter — the specification is purely data-derived, which means it's more exposed to overfitting risk than a theory-driven pick would be. I chose a wide standard deviation (0.40) to reflect genuine uncertainty about the decay, while centering the mean (0.55) at roughly half the in-sample value — consistent with typical shrinkage seen when modest, shallow searches (3 moves, not an exhaustive grid) are evaluated out-of-sample.

I did not hit any of my stop/restart triggers explicitly (gains stayed above the 0.02 restart threshold, no failures occurred, and Sharpe stayed below my 1.2 stop bar), but I reached the hard limit of 3 content moves allowed this session, so I proceeded to submit with the strongest result found.
